**A table is a relationship structure, not just a collection of text boxes.** The value “17” is meaningful only when associated with the correct row label and column header. Merged headers, missing borders, rotated text, and multiple scripts make those relationships difficult to infer. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.10683)

A box-and-graph system predicts cells and relations such as adjacency or shared row/column membership. Its strength is explicit geometry. Its challenge is turning possibly inconsistent pairwise relations into one coherent grid. A sequence system instead emits HTML or a compact table grammar, representing spans and order as tokens.

**One small error can change many meanings.** If a header spans three columns but the model predicts a span of two, later values can be attached to the wrong category even when every character is recognized correctly. A sequence decoder can produce valid syntax yet an incorrect layout; a graph model can find good boxes yet connect them wrongly.

Validate cell occupancy, spans, row lengths, and reading order. Use high-resolution crops while retaining enough page context to identify titles and headers. Report results by difficult table type rather than only a pooled average. When diagnosing a failure, separate structure reconstruction from text recognition so you improve the component that actually caused the wrong association.

**Technical details and references.**

Spanning cells break a simple one-box-per-grid-slot assumption; borderless tables require alignment cues; rotation changes geometry; mixed scripts complicate recognition and reading order. Box-plus-graph methods predict cells and relations such as same-row/column or adjacency, preserving explicit geometry. Sequence methods generate HTML or a compact structural grammar such as OTSL. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.10683)

Graph methods need consistent relation decoding; sequence methods can produce syntactically valid but geometrically inconsistent tables or drift after one token error. Separate structure from text recognition when diagnosing failures. Validate rowspan/colspan coverage, nonoverlapping cell occupancy, row lengths, and reading order.

Use high-resolution crops with global page context and evaluate difficult table categories separately. A table that looks plausible visually may still attach a value to the wrong header, which is often the consequential error.
